title: The End of the Jesus Era (An Investigation, #1)
author: Ralph Ellis
target_audience: Scholars of religious studies and ancient history
Individuals curious about alternative biblical interpretations
core_themes: Alternative interpretations of New Testament events
Relationship between Roman and Jewish histories
Origins of Christian doctrine and myth
primary_purpose: To critically investigate the historical reality of Jesus and the early Christian narrative, challenging traditional accounts and suggesting alternative explanations rooted in documented history.

structure_format.organization: Chapters explore historical records, parallel narratives, and discrepancies between canonical texts and external sources
features: Use of non-canonical sources and archaeology

key_concepts_lessons: The traditional story of Jesus may be based on misunderstood or misrepresented history.
Canonical gospels contain inconsistencies when compared to external historical sources.
Alternative readings of ancient texts can shed new light on the origins of Christianity.
Roman and Jewish political contexts significantly shaped the development of Christian doctrine.
Critical investigation of religious history can reveal overlooked connections and motives.
notable_features: Focuses on historiographical critique rather than faith-based analysis
Draws parallels between Jesus and other figures within the same era
First volume in a series investigating biblical history
cultural_historical_context: Emerges from a tradition of skeptical biblical scholarship in the 21st century, responding to growing interest in revisiting foundational religious narratives using historical methods.
reception_impact: Supported by some in the alternative history and secular scholarship communities
Controversial among theologians and traditional believers
Praised for thorough research and bold hypotheses
Criticized for speculative conclusions and challenging established beliefs
comparable_titles: Misquoting Jesus by Bart D. Ehrman
Zealot: The Life and Times of Jesus of Nazareth by Reza Aslan
